standard: CCSS.MATH.CONTENT.6.G.A.1 (area of right triangles and other triangles by composing them into rectangles; other polygons are later missions)
source: Original content written for Pip, aligned to CCSS.MATH.CONTENT.6.G.A.1. No textbook or published lesson was used.
attribution: None required (original content). The standard is cited by its code only.
in_scope: area of a triangle when the base and height are given
putting two copies of a triangle together to make a rectangle or parallelogram
area of a rectangle as base × height (the root skill)
comparing the areas of two triangles
the height goes straight up from the base, not along a slanted side (only if the student brings it up)
out_of_scope: area of a parallelogram as its own formula (next mission)
finding a missing base or height from the area

look_fors: Says two identical copies of the triangle fit together into a rectangle or parallelogram (one sentence is enough)
The shape they make has the same base and height as the triangle (may be implied)
probe_ladder: why is that wrong? it has a base and a height, so i multiplied them.
if my 6 by 4 triangle sits in a 6 by 4 box, does it fill the whole box?
what's in the empty part of the box? same shape as my triangle?
then a skinny triangle and a 6 by 4 box take up the same space. that's what my rule says.
concepts.friend_nudge: My cousin said she cut a paper sandwich corner to corner and both pieces matched…? I don't know what that has to do with triangles.
concepts.aha: oh, two of them make a box
concrete: what if i cut my 6 by 4 box corner to corner, what do i get?
connections: ohh so it's like cutting a pizza box corner to corner?

look_fors: Multiplies base by height for the rectangle on one example (6 × 4 = 24)
Walks the example, or corrects Pip's wrong prediction (like adding 6 + 4)
probe_ladder: how big is the shape they make together?
walk me through a 6 by 4 rectangle. how do you get its area?
i'll guess a 6 by 4 rectangle is 6 + 4 = 10 squares. is that right?
then a 6 by 4 rectangle and a 6 by 4 triangle are both 24. that's what my rule says.
concepts.friend_nudge: Someone in my class said she counts the squares row by row instead of one at a time…? That seems faster.
concepts.aha: ok so the box is just base times height
concrete: what if i cover a 6 by 4 box with 1 by 1 squares, how many do i need?

look_fors: Says one triangle is half of the rectangle because two of them make it (one sentence is enough, and it can build on an earlier message)
Applies it: base × height ÷ 2 on an example (6 × 4 ÷ 2 = 12)
probe_ladder: why would a triangle get less than base times height?
does a 6 by 4 triangle cover all 24 squares of a 6 by 4 box?
is a triangle with base 8 and height 3 bigger than one with base 6 and height 4?
then a triangle covering part of a 6 by 4 box is still 24, same as the whole box. that's what my rule says.
concepts.friend_nudge: My friend said to think about sharing one tray of brownies with exactly one other person…? I don't know why she was hungry.
concepts.aha: ohh so the triangle is just half the box
concrete: what if i fold the 6 by 4 box corner to corner, how many squares sit on each side?
connections: so it's like sharing one sandwich with a friend, you each get the same bit?

offline_demo.note: Maya's main demo (CONTRACT v3.6). Pip's opening is the server's templated claim: 'I'm learning area of a triangle. I already know one rule: Area of a triangle is base times height, so a 6 by 4 triangle is 24. Easy.' Turns 1-3 are three one-sentence texts that bring every concept to level 2 (ready for quiz). Turn 4 is the deliberate wrong rule (heal) that makes Pip miss the right-triangle question; turn 5 is the re-teach (level 3: applied to the new case). 'rung' is the 1-based probe_ladder rung Pip ends the reply on, for 'next_concept_id'. 'also' lists other concepts the same message moves. Every quote after 'Saving that:' is a verbatim substring of that turn's student message. PACE-1: every Pip reply is at most 2 short sentences besides the 'Saving that' filing, a 'so you're saying' paraphrase appears at most every other turn (8 words max), nothing already given is re-asked, and the turn marked ready_for_quiz ends with 'ok i think i get it. quiz me?'.

turns.pip: oh, half. so my 24 was too big? does my triangle not fill the whole 6 by 4 box?
ohh two of mine make the box. how big is the box?
12, so half the 24 box. ok i think i get it. quiz me?

turns.student: oh but for a right triangle you just times the two sides
turns.filed_rule: for a right triangle you just times the two sides
turns.pip: Saving that: 'for a right triangle you just times the two sides'. a special rule for corners, ok.

turns.pip_ask: my brain has a bug. help me fix it: what's the area of a right triangle with base 10 and height 5?
turns.student: no a right triangle is still half a rectangle so its 10×5÷2 = 25
turns.filed_rule: a right triangle is still half a rectangle
turns.pip: ohh so corners don't change it, still half the box. throwing out my corner rule.

quiz.pip_answer: A rectangle with base 6 and height 4.
quiz.line: A rectangle, base 6 and height 4. You said 2 triangles make a rectangle.
10 times 5. 50. Same as your 6 times 4, just bigger.
Your rule for right triangles: times the two sides. 10 × 5 = 50, which is the whole rectangle. Following your rule anyway. 😵

retry.line: The whole 10 by 5 rectangle is 50. A right triangle is still half of it, so 25.
